recognize_zh: 骨髓切片低倍下可見兩個邊界清楚的圓形類上皮組織球團（epithelioid granuloma），外圍有小淋巴球環繞；但此放大倍率下中央未見明確的無細胞嗜伊紅乾酪樣壞死，是否為乾酪性肉芽腫需以高倍確認並做抗酸染色。
features: Low-power trephine with bony trabeculae, fat and hemorrhagic, variably cellular marrow
Two well-circumscribed nodular aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and elongated nuclei
Peripheral cuff of small lymphocytes around the granulomas and an adjacent lymphoid infiltrate
Central caseous necrosis is not clearly identified at this magnification; no definite multinucleated giant cells resolved
Residual hematopoietic elements scattered between fat spaces
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy at low power shows two well-formed, circumscribed epithelioid granulomas composed of histiocytes with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and elongated nuclei, rimmed by small lymphocytes. The intervening marrow shows fat, hemorrhage and scattered residual hematopoiesis. A definite central zone of amorphous acellular caseous necrosis is not appreciated at this magnification, and giant cells are not clearly resolved. Findings are consistent with granulomatous inflammation of the marrow; caseation should be confirmed at higher power, and AFB and fungal stains with cultures are recommended given the association with mycobacterial infection.

ddx.vs: Sarcoid-type granulomas are compact, epithelioid and lack central necrosis, whereas caseating granulomas have an acellular granular eosinophilic center.
Lipogranulomas are small, contain lipid vacuoles within histiocytes and lack a lymphocytic cuff or necrosis.
A polymorphous infiltrate with eosinophils, fibrosis and CD30+/CD15+ Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells distinguishes lymphoma-associated granulomas.
Morphology overlaps; GMS/PAS stains show yeasts, whereas mycobacteria require Ziehl-Neelsen or culture/PCR.
